finding.claim: Verifier accepts unsigned tokens when the configured key is an empty string or null and an algorithms allowlist is set.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token with an empty signature segment; precondition is the app passing key '' or null with algorithms set (e.g. unset-but-defined env var).
finding.sink: Signature verification skipped in validateAlgorithmAndSignature, so any payload is accepted.

trace.note: Type check admits null (typeof null === 'object') and '' (string).
Falsy key skips key preparation; key remains '' or null.
hasKey = !!key evaluates to false.
missingSignature / missingKey checks do not fire when neither key nor signature is present.
Empty signature segment passes the base64url regex.
validateAlgorithmAndSignature called with empty signature.
'if (signature && ...)' skips signature verification.

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist at verifier.js:162 (passes for configured alg). With no algorithms configured, verifier.js:502-504 makes the list empty and rejects everything, so the bug needs the algorithms option set. Signer rejects empty keys (signer.js:216) but verifier does not.

finding.claim: Optional-claim validators (aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce, iat/maxAge, exp, nbf) are skipped when the claim is absent, so a verifier expecting an audience accepts validly signed tokens lacking aud.
finding.source: Token signed by the trusted key that omits the claim (e.g. login token or token from another service sharing the key).
finding.sink: Audience/issuer/subject/expiry enforcement configured by the verifier.

trace.note: allowedAud pushes an aud validator.
maxAge pushes an iat validator; exp validator at 606-614.
Validator loop runs each validator.
If !(claim in payload), executes continue and skips the check.
Presence is only enforced if requiredClaims is configured, and it is optional.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification (verifier.js:280) passes for the issuer-signed token. requiredClaims (verifier.js:293-299) is optional and not enforced by default. Comment at verifier.js:310 assumes requiredClaims covers presence.

finding.claim: Signature segment is not checked for canonical base64url encoding, so one signature has multiple valid token strings (trailing-bit malleability); ECDSA high-S form also verifies. Verifier comment claims the signature is canonical, which is false.
finding.source: Attacker alters trailing bits / encoding of the signature segment of a previously seen valid token.
finding.sink: Token string accepted by the verifier; matters where the app keys revocation, replay, or one-time-use on the raw token string.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE checks alphabet only.
Signature segment checked only against the alphabet regex.
Comment claims signature is canonical after decoder check; not true.
Buffer.from(signature, 'base64') ignores unused trailing bits, so distinct strings decode to same bytes.
timingSafeEqual on decoded bytes accepts every variant.

finding.guards_checked: Base64url charset regex (decoder.js:10). Timing-safe HMAC comparison (crypto.js:343). Depends on Node base64 decoding ignoring trailing bits, believed correct but not executed.

finding.claim: On the async path, complete:true returns input as the full token including signature, not the signing input, unlike the sync path.
finding.source: Caller uses verifier with complete:true and async key fetcher.
finding.sink: Returned input field used by caller for manual signature recomputation.

trace.note: Async success returns input: token (full token).
Sync success path returns input from decode, the signing input.
Decoder slices input as token.slice(0, lastSeparator).

finding.guards_checked: None needed for the bug itself; most downstream code fails closed on mismatch.

finding.claim: Falsy crit values (empty string, false, 0, null) skip RFC 7515 crit validation, so non-compliant tokens are accepted.
finding.source: Issuer-signed token with crit set to a falsy non-array value.
finding.sink: Token accepted despite invalid crit header.

trace.note: if (!header.crit) return exits before validation.
Non-empty array check would have rejected the value.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification runs before validateCrit (verifier.js:280, 283). Attacker needs a valid signature, so impact is spec conformance.

finding.claim: Signer header option can override alg via spread, so the header alg can differ from the algorithm used to sign.
finding.source: Untrusted data passed as the header option to createSigner (application misuse).
finding.sink: Token header alg that disagrees with the signing algorithm.

trace.note: header built with alg: algorithm.
...additionalHeader spread overrides alg.
Signature computed with algorithm variable, not header.alg.
Async path signs with detected algorithm.

finding.guards_checked: None in the library. Requires untrusted header input to the signer.

finding.claim: With an HS-only algorithms list, a PEM public key is used as an HMAC secret without a key-type check, so anyone holding the public key can forge HS256 tokens.
finding.source: Precondition: app passes an RSA/EC public key PEM with algorithms ['HS256']; attacker holds the public key.
finding.sink: HMAC verification keyed with public key bytes, accepting forged tokens.

trace.note: detectPublicKeyAlgorithms(key, allowedAlgorithms) called with HS-only list.
HS-only list returns early, skipping PEM detection.
prepareKeyOrSecret(key, true) chosen because detected alg is HS.
createSecretKey on PEM bytes with no key-type check.
HMAC over PEM text verifies forged token.

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist (verifier.js:162) passes for HS256. checkAreCompatibleAlgorithms (verifier.js:519) passes. Code comment at crypto.js:260 says this is intentional, so it is a configuration footgun rather than a plain bug.

finding.claim: Private-key detection cache is keyed only by key string and ignores providedAlgorithm, so a cached HS result is returned for later calls with a different algorithm.
finding.source: Signer called first with a PEM key and HS algorithm, then with the same key and a different (or omitted) algorithm, in the same process.
finding.sink: Signer algorithm selection: throws on mismatch, or assigns HS256 to a PEM private key when algorithm is omitted.

trace.note: HS providedAlgorithm returned early inside performDetect.
Result cached under key string only.
Cache lookup ignores providedAlgorithm.
Stale HS result causes checkIsCompatibleAlgorithm to throw for RS/ES requests.
With algorithm omitted, stale HS256 is assigned and PEM bytes used as HMAC secret.

finding.guards_checked: checkIsCompatibleAlgorithm (signer.js:155) catches some mismatches but not the omitted-algorithm case. Signer-side only; low impact.
